title: Fade integrated SubD detail continuously across a curved host

defect: support loops propagated across the whole host

preconditions: the feature physically belongs to the host surface rather than being a separate assembly
the broad host silhouette and radial density are already sufficient
the feature can reach zero depth in a low-stress region
required_observations: base cage connectivity and radial/longitudinal spacing
fixed MatCap views that cross the feature fade
a second view when the feature is nearly tangent to the first camera
action_policy: Keep the feature connected to the host cage and ramp its depth through multiple rings rather than switching from zero to full depth on one ring.
When the feature changes lateral direction, blend influence across neighboring columns instead of jumping the active column between adjacent rings.
Terminate or dissolve support flow only where the feature is already flush and the evaluated highlight stays continuous.
Prefer 12-16 radial segments at ordinary prop scale unless silhouette or highlight evidence requires more.
failure_predicates: global density added for one local feature
candidate metrics accepted without visual confirmation
recovery: move termination into a flatter or lower-stress region
rebuild the local flow instead of patching repeated pinches

sources.description: Josh - Blender Bros reroutes the detail boundary, creates a local buffer, fades depth to flush, terminates flow, and relaxes curved spacing.

experiments.counterevidence: Raw pinch-candidate count increased from 26 to 32 in the visually better source-like correction, so it cannot be used as a standalone gate.

runtime_usage.usage: Author one connected ring-based cage with local per-segment radial and vertical offsets; keep Solidify/SubD live.

version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS reproduction; source reports Blender 4.2.0
status_note: Validated on a source-like 16-segment tapered shell and a different 14-segment oval cuff. Exact local triangle termination remains bounded by the companion topology-sheet experiment.
